heroHeadline: May Jobs +172K Blowout (June 5) Triggers 'Good News = Bad News' — S&P –1.2%, 10Y 4.54%, December Fed Hike Fully Priced; ISM Services 54.5 + ADP +122K (June 3); Section 301 Tariffs 60 Economies; Warsh FOMC 11 Days; Iran MOU Unsigned Day 7
heroSubtitle: The May 2026 Non-Farm Payrolls report released June 5 delivered a historic blowout: +172,000 jobs against an ~85,000 consensus, with unemployment holding at 4.3% and prior months revised up a combined +93,000. The report confirmed that the US labor market is not in recession — the Sahm Rule indicator remains at ~0.43%, below the 0.5% recession-signal threshold, and mass layoffs have not materialized despite tariff uncertainty and the Iran war energy shock. However, the blowout triggered an immediate 'good news is bad news' market reaction: the S&P 500 fell ~1.2% to approximately 7,493, the 10-year Treasury yield surged to 4.54%, and traders fully priced a 25bp rate hike by December 2026 for the first time in the Warsh era. The Nasdaq dropped 1.1–1.8% as AI chip names sold off sharply (Micron –6.3%, AMD –6.3%, Broadcom –3.8% on unchanged guidance). On June 3, ISM Services PMI for May came in at 54.5% — beating the 53.8% forecast with Prices Paid at 71.3% (highest since August 2022) — while ADP private payrolls showed +122,000 (beat), validating the Friday blowout. The US Trade Representative simultaneously proposed Section 301 tariffs of 10–12.5% on approximately 60 economies, citing forced labor practices — the next tariff wave designed to survive the Section 122 cliff on July 24 (49 days). The Iran nuclear MOU remains unsigned on Day 7 as Trump returned the draft seeking stronger language on uranium enrichment timelines and Hormuz control handover; VP Vance acknowledged signing remains uncertain. Brent crude fell from ~$101 (June 3) to ~$97 (June 5) on continued deal optimism. Goldman Sachs recession probability is expected to revise below 25% (from 25% on May 11) following the jobs blowout; JPMorgan and Moody's Analytics updates are pending. The new risk scenario emerging is 'no landing' — growth above trend with inflation above 2% target — which would require the Warsh Fed to hike rather than cut, with implications across equity valuations (CAPE ~39), bond yields (30Y above 5%), and mortgage rates (~7.5%). Kevin Warsh's inaugural FOMC on June 16–17 is now 11 days away; the simultaneous Bank of Japan rate hike decision (65–77% probability to 1.00%) creates a potential dual-central-bank shock of the August 2024 'Black Monday II' type.
footerNote: Data sourced from: BLS — Employment Situation May 2026, NFP +172K / unemployment 4.3% (released June 5, 2026); Yahoo Finance — S&P 500 –1.2%, Nasdaq selloff, 10Y 4.54% (June 5, 2026); ISM — Services PMI May 2026, 54.5% (released June 3, 2026); ADP — National Employment Report May 2026, +122K private payrolls (released June 3, 2026); CNBC — Section 301 Tariffs ~60 economies 10–12.5% (June 3, 2026); Fortune — Oil price June 3–5, 2026 (Brent $97–101); Axios — Iran MOU tentative framework, signing uncertain as of June 5.
